title: "Is Your Profile Underperforming?" — the niche's biggest proven ad
note: 195 days live, 521,572 EU reach on 2026-09-06 (510,116 on 09-02) — the hardest public number in the niche. Mechanism: a neutral diagnostic question instead of an insult, then 'data-driven profile review' as the free first step. Proof that the compliance-safe variant out-delivers the personal-attributes one. And proof that the cut decides: its 0:27 sibling with identical copy (1374983617735721) sits at 15,530.

title: SWAY — longest-living ad in the niche (197 days)
note: Running since 2026-02-17. Mechanism: rate → fix → generate bundle in one sentence ('rates your profile, polishes your photos, delivers top-tier hinge prompts'). Opens with a personal-attributes question we must not copy — study the offer stack, not the hook.

title: "You're not ugly. Your photos are just terrible."
note: 189 days live, 50,758 EU reach (2026-09-06); the family (8 ads, 0:21–1:14) totals ~90k — the weakest of Charmd's three families in delivery, though it survives. Mechanism: insult-then-absolve — the blame moves from the man to his photos, 'no fake filters, no weird AI look' answers the likeness objection in-copy. Second-person appearance framing = Meta policy risk we do not copy.

title: "Better Photos. More Matches." — the clean variant
note: 179 days live, 61,355 EU reach (2026-09-06); the family (4 ads) totals ~99k. Mechanism: same photos-are-the-problem angle compressed to four beats — 'No studio. No cringe. Just more right swipes.' Closest existing ad to our voice rules; the benchmark to beat with coached-pose + free-check.

title: "Same face. 10x the matches." — Roast's top ad by impressions
note: Ran 2026-04-24 → 2026-09-02 (131 days), #1 on Roast's page by impressions while it lived; the 'Same face' family (~257 ads) keeps running with new variants. Mechanism: third-person coworker-gatekeeping story + a phone-screenshot IMAGE of a full Hinge match list as the creative — social proof shown, not claimed. Low-fi static beats their polished video. The '10x' multiplier is an invented stat we never copy.

title: "If you're between 25 and 34 and can't get more than 1 match a week"
note: 123 days live (2026-09-06). Mechanism: explicit age-bracket callout of exactly our ICP + 'it's not your face, it's your photos' reframe + free 2-minute first step. Interesting: qualifying the audience in copy instead of only in targeting. Side-market read: 782 UK accounts in four months (England only) — Roast's money is in the US.

title: "We are looking for 30 guys who open Tinder and get zero matches"
note: 107 days live. Mechanism: casting-call format — scarcity and selection without a fake countdown. The viewer applies rather than buys. A borrowable third-person structure.

title: ReGen control copy — one text, ~98 video variants
note: 54 days live and replicated across ~98 active variants — scaling by replication, not by one old ad. Mechanism: benefit inventory in plain third person ('no photographer, no outfit planning, no asking a friend'), Meta-safe throughout. The compliance template for app-install copy in this niche.

title: "She swiped left before she even got to your bio" — Photoshoot Dating
note: Ran 2026-07-21 → 2026-09-17 and is now inactive — 58 days, not the living veteran the 2026-09-02 read called it (re-checked 2026-09-21). Mechanism: the 100-ms-decision moment dramatized ("girls decide in half a second and it's your photos making the call, not your face"), then "that part's fixable". Same territory as our locked line "She decided in 100 ms." What we take is the mechanism; what we do not take is the form — "she swiped left before she even got to your bio" and the headline "fix your photos now" are second-person claims about the viewer's dating results, which is the PRODUCT.md §11 personal-attributes line. It is also worth asking whether that is what stopped it.

title: "roast generated 10/10 photos from his selfies" — Roast's scaling wave, UGC
note: Live since 2026-08-30, 0:50 UGC video, 'Use AI to get more matches / No photographer needed'. One of seven variants of a single concept launched 2026-08-26 → 08-31 — the category leader scaling AI photos as the front door instead of the quiz. Mechanism: third-person story about him (dead profile → generated photos from selfies → inbox), the product named late, a two-minute first step. Unproven by longevity (days, not months) and its outcome claims ('matches won't stop texting', '10/10') are not ours; the shape is: he, his photos, no photographer.

title: "Most guys blame Tinder. The problem is the photos." — the blame-shift, static
note: Live since 2026-05-06 (123 days on 2026-09-06); a direct-response card, Tinder ✗ vs ROAST ✓. Mechanism: the blame moves from the app to the photos in one line, then a small first step ('Upload 4 and Roast tells you exactly what to fix in 2 minutes'). The reframe every winner in the niche shares — the model for our campaign 5, minus any diagnosis of the viewer.

title: "Stop blaming the algorithm" — a 12-second silent screen recording
note: Live since 2026-06-11 (87 days), 0:12, no voice, captions only — one of the three longest-running videos on the Roast page and the format the teardown scored 'Brief it'. Mechanism: 'the reason is sitting in your photos and you can't see it' → the free two-minute quiz. We take the silent format and the blame-shift; the 'you're getting no matches' diagnosis stays theirs.
